headline: Agents go to work: marketing to machines, robots as APIs, and selling outcomes not seats.

models.name: B2A marketing: selling to AI agents, not humans
models.technique: Query the major AI assistants for how they describe your company to each buying-group member, trace which sources inform their answers, and flag anonymous AI-driven traffic at the account level. Productize it as an 'AEO Agent' (answer-engine optimization) plus campaign and audience agents, reachable through APIs and MCP so marketers query it from inside their own assistants.
models.what_it_is: Marketing built for an audience of AI assistants: track how agents describe and recommend your brand, find the sources behind their answers, and reach buyers through the agents that now intermediate B2B purchasing.
models.who: Demandbase (launched Oct 20 at GO conference; 342M contacts, 13M companies).
models.why_emerging: Demandbase cites a Gartner prediction that AI agents will intermediate 90% of B2B buying by 2028. When the buyer asks an AI, the brand that the AI describes wins — a new surface to measure and optimize.

models.name: Physical-asset AI with government anchor contracts
models.technique: Build simulation and monitoring models for operators of complex physical systems; sell disruption forecasting, not licenses. Land anchor government contracts first — ASI's five-year $99M Army deal and 12-year $875M FAA deal — then expand the same playbook into energy and logistics. The pitch is reliability arithmetic, not vibes.
models.what_it_is: AI that forecasts disruptions hours, days or weeks ahead across air traffic, power grids and military operations — software that manages physical systems, sold on the outcome of fewer surprises.
models.who: ASI (Boston; $325M Series C at $3B, led by Spark Capital; CEO Phillip Buckendorf).
models.why_emerging: Investor appetite is shifting from text-generating AI to AI that controls physical assets; agencies will pay long contracts for reliability in critical infrastructure.

models.name: Robot foundation model sold as an API
models.technique: Wrap the model in a developer API with the same ergonomics as an LLM call; add a fine-tuning service on small customer demo datasets; remove the hardware barrier with a browser playground that drives a real robot remotely. Sell per-hour compute ($3/hr primary, ~$0.75/hr flash per Forbes, unconfirmed) and let usage data improve the model centrally.
models.what_it_is: A cross-embodiment robot brain: send a live camera feed plus a plain-English instruction ('pick up the cup'), get back motor commands — working on robot hardware the model never trained on.
models.who: Dream Labs (SF; $90M seed, B Capital/Kindred; 20+ hardware partners; ex-Nvidia team).
models.why_emerging: VCs now treat robot foundation models as an extension of the AI buildout, not a separate hardware bet; if one model drives any manufacturer's robot, proprietary control software loses its moat.

models.name: Synthetic user research: modeled customers on demand
models.technique: Build behavior models (SAPIENS-style) from real-user data, expose them as a test panel marketers and designers can run simulations against, and report results with confidence framing. Keep a live-test holdout as validation so finance still signs off. Seed customers in health-adjacent verticals (GoodRx, MIDI Health) prove the wedge.
models.what_it_is: Instead of recruiting human panels, test your campaign, product flow or customer-facing AI agent against a simulated audience built from behavioral models — and get a first read in minutes.
models.who: Vectorial (SF; $3M seed Oct 20; 2.5M modeled people, 30K+ simulations run).
models.why_emerging: Teams want fast signal before paying for live tests; behavior models now claim to reproduce prior user-study findings with 85%+ accuracy, making synthetic panels a credible pre-launch layer.

models.name: Outcome-based pricing for AI agents
models.technique: Evolve pricing with the product: start with a single billable outcome (Intercom's Fin: per resolved conversation), add billable outcomes as the agent does more, and let customers pre-commit to credit pools drawn down across outcomes. Make spend predictable — dashboards, limits, forecasts — because predictability is now part of the product. Price the value, treat tokens as pass-through.
models.what_it_is: Stop selling seats and tokens: charge for completed work — the resolved support conversation, the booked meeting, the task done — with subscriptions and credits layered around it.
models.who: Intercom's Fin, Replit, Clay (via Stripe Monetize 2026; Orb data: 95% hybrid adoption).
models.why_emerging: AI's variable costs break flat pricing, and buyers increasingly pay for outcomes; two-thirds of the Forbes AI 50 now use some usage-based pricing as agents make 'per seat' meaningless.

signal: The customer is becoming a machine: agents buy the software, drive the robots, sit on the research panel — and get billed by outcome. Build for the agent as the buyer and the user.
